answer: Physical security tokens deter Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to unclonable material tags. A node proves identity by illuminating a substrate embedded with luminescent pigment using an excitation lantern, while a micro-mechanical quill measures fine surface contours. Attackers must fund specialized nanolithography per forged node, imposing steep capital costs. However, probe friction steadily abrades the substrate, eventually causing false rejections during verification.
